Grand Army Plaza entrance.description: Grand Army Plaza is Prospect Park's monumental northern entrance and a major transit arrival; use the arch and plaza to orient toward Long Meadow and park paths.

Prospect Park Ravine and Waterfall.description: The Ravine is a wooded interior landscape with streams, bridges, and waterfalls; paths include slopes, steps, mud, and limited nighttime visibility.

New York Hall of Science and Rocket Park.description: The New York Hall of Science and Rocket Park are separately ticketed, staffed attractions with their own entrance, calendar, accessibility services, and hours.

Flushing Meadows Aquatic Center.description: The Aquatic Center is a staffed recreation facility whose pool, rink, membership requirements, closures, and reopening status must be checked separately from the park.

Diller-von Furstenberg Sundeck and Water.description: The sundeck and seasonal water feature provide seating and a place to cool feet along the elevated route; water operation varies with weather and maintenance.

Chelsea Thicket.description: Chelsea Thicket is a densely planted, quieter passage that shows the High Line's rail landscape; the narrow route can become crowded and has limited shade seating.

Pershing Square Beams.description: Pershing Square Beams is the family play area where the structure exposes the High Line's steel framework; play access and water elements may be seasonal.

Pier 3 Greenway Terrace and labyrinth.description: Pier 3 combines a planted terrace, exploratory labyrinth, lawns, and harbor views; its quieter paths sit between the busier Pier 2 and Pier 5 activity zones.

Pier 4 Beach.description: Pier 4 Beach is a small engineered shoreline for observing the tidal river and launching approved programs; it is not a swimming beach.

Pier 26 and Science Playground.description: Pier 26 combines river ecology interpretation, an accessible marine-science playground, lawns, and recreation; programmed areas and concessions keep separate schedules.

Bosque Fountain and gardens.description: The Bosque is a shaded garden with seating and a seasonal fountain near the park's eastern side; fountain operation can change with weather and maintenance.

Battery Urban Farm.description: Battery Urban Farm is an educational growing space with scheduled programs rather than a general pick-your-own garden; stay on public paths and respect closures.

Peter Minuit Plaza.description: Peter Minuit Plaza is the major subway, bus, ferry, and bike arrival on the park's east side; it is busy and works best as an orientation and meeting point.

Bryant Park public restroom.description: The staffed public restroom near the northeast corner is a valuable visitor amenity, but queues and temporary cleaning closures are common at busy times.

Fountain Terrace.description: The Josephine Shaw Lowell Memorial Fountain terrace is a central meeting and seating area near Sixth Avenue, with seasonal food kiosks and event activity nearby.

Petanque courts.description: The gravel petanque courts host casual and organized play along the western side; scheduled leagues and events may take priority over drop-in use.

Outlook Hill.description: Outlook Hill is the island's highest viewpoint, reached by sloped paths and steps, with harbor and skyline views but little weather protection at the top.

Colonels Row.description: Colonels Row is a shaded historic district used for festivals, art, and seasonal programs; building interiors and event footprints are not always open.

Soldiers and Sailors Monument.description: The Soldiers and Sailors Monument is a prominent civic landmark near West 89th Street; interior access is limited and surrounding steps are not the accessible route.

Riverside Skate Park.description: Riverside Skate Park is a dedicated wheel-sport area in the northern park corridor; surfaces, supervision, and seasonal operations should be checked before a special trip.
